problem: Self-supervised image representations are usually learned from pretext tasks on static photo collections and target semantic recognition. Prior interaction-based feature learning used touch or egomotion. No prior work learned visual features from actively emitted sound, and generic or semantically supervised pre-training is poorly matched to spatial tasks such as depth, surface normals and point-goal navigation.
motivation: Echoes are a function of the same latent 3D geometry that the camera observes, so actively emitting a chirp and listening to the binaural response gives free, interaction-based supervision about spatial layout; bats and blind humans exploit exactly this. A case study in simulated Replica scenes shows that depth can be predicted from echoes alone (better than a mean-depth baseline) and that echoes improve RGB-based depth. This suggests echoes can teach a visual encoder spatial cues that remain useful when no audio is available at test time.
key_idea: Pre-train an RGB encoder by making it predict which of four relative orientations (same / right 90° / opposite / left 90°) a binaural echo, recorded at the same location, came from. This forces the visual features to encode 3D layout consistent with the acoustics. The encoder is then used audio-free for depth, surface normals and PointGoal navigation.
insight: Aligning the pretext task with the target task family matters more than label supervision. On Replica depth (UNet), the echo-orientation pre-training (RMS 0.332) beats both ImageNet (0.356) and MIT-Indoor-supervised (0.334) initializations. On PointNav, MIT-Indoor scene-classification pre-training actually hurts relative to scratch (SPL 0.798 vs 0.830), while VisualEchoes improves it (0.856) and roughly halves the final distance to goal vs MIT-Indoor. Ablations show that the hard, same-position 4-way orientation task is key: it beats a 2-class simplification (RMS 0.340) and an AVC-style same/different-environment BinaryMatching task (RMS 0.345). This indicates that fine-grained geometric (dis)agreement between view and echo, not mere audio-visual correspondence, drives the spatial features. The pretext task itself reaches 66% accuracy (chance 25%).
method: Echolocation simulation: reuse SoundSpaces' pre-computed binaural RIRs on Habitat+Replica. Source and receiver are co-located at every navigable grid point (0.5 m) facing 4 cardinal directions. The emitted chirp is a 3 ms 20 Hz–20 kHz sweep convolved with the RIR to give left/right echoes; the first 60 ms at 44.1 kHz is kept and converted to an STFT (Hann 64, hop 16, FFT 512).

Case study (RGB+Echo2Depth / Echo2Depth / RGB2Depth): a multimodal U-Net predicts 128×128 depth from RGB plus echo spectrogram, echo only, or RGB only. It quantifies how much spatial information echoes carry.

VisualEchoes pretext network: a visual stream on the current RGB view and an audio stream on the echo from one of the 4 orientations at the same position. The two features are concatenated and passed through an FC fusion layer (D=128), then a 4-way FC classifier (↑ same, → right 90°, ↓ opposite, ← left 90°) trained with cross-entropy. Mismatched pairs are hard negatives because they come from the same location.

Audio-free transfer: the pretrained visual encoder is swapped in as the RGB backbone for three tasks: the RGB2Depth UNet encoder, ResNet-50 in Hu et al.'s multi-scale depth network, PSPNet for surface normals, and the 3-layer CNN of the Habitat PPO PointGoal agent (then trained end-to-end with RL).
Baselines/ablations: ImageNet-supervised, MIT-Indoor-Scenes-supervised, scratch initialization, SimpleVisualEchoes (2-class) and BinaryMatching (same-environment AVC-style).

results: On RGB PointGoal navigation in unseen Replica scenes, VisualEchoes pre-training gives SPL 0.856, distance-to-goal 0.476 and normalized DTG 0.061. This beats scratch (0.830/0.728/0.096), ImageNet-supervised (0.833/0.663/0.081) and MIT-Indoor-supervised (0.798/1.05/0.124) initializations. For surface normals on NYU-V2 it beats ImageNet pre-training (mean angle error 22.9° vs 26.4°). On depth it consistently beats scratch across Replica/NYU-V2/DIODE and rivals MIT-Indoor-supervised pre-training. With the ResNet-50 Hu et al. depth model it still trails ImageNet pre-training (RMS 0.683 vs 0.555).
limitations: Echoes are purely simulated (SoundSpaces RIRs on only 18 Replica scenes) with only 4 discrete orientations; real-robot echo capture is left to future work.

The navigation evaluation is a single small-scale Replica PointGoal experiment with an RGB-only agent: no Gibson/MP3D/HM3D benchmark and no variance reported. Gains over ImageNet are modest (SPL +2.3 points).
It does not beat ImageNet-supervised ResNet-50 for NYU-V2 depth in the strong Hu et al. pipeline. Chirp emission is fixed rather than actively chosen.
